findings: The flag requires at-most mode and profile=nonstar, so ownership variables are constructed.
Each candidate bad owned-edge pair is guarded by the negation of the target flag captured before that gate; this admits gates up to and including the first exact output and excludes later gates.
On a triangle-free graph, existence of two disjoint owned edges is equivalent to failure of star profile. Earlier gates/cones/ownership are unchanged when taking the prefix.
The decoder separately confirms the earliest exact prefix on every assignment and requires its profile to be nonstar.
With the option disabled, all model constraints are unchanged. The guardian delta only extends the encoder allowlist.
scope: Source audit only, no solver result. A nonstar exact prefix is not a minimum-circuit witness and does not refute existence of an equally small star-profile circuit. Signed-domination normalization remains only a necessary condition for global minima, not a complete enumeration of all nonminimum nonstar circuits.
